items.q: MPGN light-microscopy findings are thickening of capillary wall, mesangial > endocapillary proliferation/hypercellularity, and:
opts: Lobular appearance of capillary tuft ± nodules (multiple small uniform nodules)
items.exp: Lobular appearance of capillary tuft ± nodules (multiple small uniform nodules). (Book p771)

items.q: The MPGN photomicrograph is captioned mesangial proliferation, with the pointer labelling:
opts: Accentuated lobular appearance of capillary duct
items.exp: Figure label: accentuated lobular appearance of capillary duct; caption mesangial proliferation. (Book p771)

items.q: The MPGN clinical-presentation split is 35% nephrotic, 35% nephritic, 20% CKD with contracted kidney and:
items.exp: 35% nephrotic; 35% nephritic; 20% CKD with contracted kidney; 10% RPGN type 2. (Book p771)

items.q: Match each MPGN presentation arm with its share — 1) Nephrotic syndrome 2) CKD with contracted kidney 3) RPGN type 2 … A) 10% B) 35% C) 20%
items.exp: Nephrotic 35%; CKD with contracted kidney 20%; RPGN type 2 10%. (Book p771)

items.q: MPGN prognosis is written as poor, with what proportion of cases heading to CKD?
The HCV extrahepatic manifestations note lists porphyria cutanea tarda, lichen planus, Sjogrens syndrome and:
items.exp: HCV extrahepatic: porphyria cutanea tarda, lichen planus, Sjogrens syndrome, cryoglobulinemia. (Book p771)

items.q: Cryoglobulinemia, in that HCV note, produces:
items.exp: Cryoglobulinemia → non thrombocytopenic palpable purpura. (Book p771)

items.q: IgA nephropathy is also known as Henoch-Schonlein nephritis and Berger's disease, and holds the tag:
items.exp: AKA Henoch-Schonlein nephritis/Berger's disease; m/c glomerular disease. (Book p771)

items.q: Match each IgA fact with its type — 1) mIgA (monomeric) production site 2) pIgA (polymeric) production site 3) pIgA normal clearance organ … A) Liver B) Bone marrow C) MALT (mucosa associated lymphoid tissue)
items.exp: mIgA produced in bone marrow; pIgA produced in MALT; normally cleared by liver. (Book p771)

items.q: Which IgA-type statement is TRUE as per the etiopathogenesis tree?
opts: Polymeric IgA is produced in MALT and is normally cleared by the liver
Monomeric IgA is produced in MALT
Polymeric IgA is produced in bone marrow
Monomeric IgA is normally cleared by the kidney
items.exp: mIgA (monomeric): bone marrow; pIgA (polymeric): MALT, normally cleared by liver. (Book p771)
